prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1413; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped at a traffic signal in Baytown, Texas, when the rear of the vehicle was struck by Driver 2, whose vehicle was travelling behind it at a low speed. Driver 1 reported neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash and stated that Passenger was also in the vehicle at the time of impact. Officers confirmed through their own observations and statements at the scene that Driver 1 and Passenger were present in the vehicle. Scene photographs show visible rear-end damage to both vehicles, although they do not show every panel or component that was reported as affected. No independent witnesses were identified, so the account relies on the statements of those involved. Driver 1 is named on the insurance policy covering the struck vehicle. Officers found no information indicating earlier damage to that vehicle. Whether all of the damage seen on the vehicle resulted from this impact could not be determined at the scene and may require further inspection.
